name: Twilio

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org (Twilio-logo-red.svg, the en.wikipedia.org Twilio infobox logo)

description: Twilio sells the plumbing that lets other companies' apps talk to their customers: developers call its software interfaces (APIs) to send text messages and WhatsApp messages, place phone calls, send email, verify logins with one-time codes, and collect customer data. Most revenue is metered: businesses pay per text sent or per minute of call, and Twilio buys the underlying delivery from phone carriers and network providers, then passes carrier fees through at cost. A smaller part (26% of 2025 revenue) is subscriptions for email (SendGrid) and the Segment customer data platform. It has about 402,000 active customer accounts, no customer above 10% of revenue, and roughly 64% of revenue from the United States. It reached a small operating profit in 2025 after years of losses.

gics.note: From the table in Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (raw wikitext read 2026-10-27): TWLO, Twilio, Information Technology, Systems Software, San Francisco, added to the index 2026-10-06. The table gives only sector and sub-industry, so industry group and industry are left null.

hq.note: 101 Spear Street, Fifth Floor, San Francisco (FY2025 10-K)

employees.note: 2,738 outside the United States; 2,632 in research and development, 2,265 in sales and marketing (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Twilio platform (single segment)
businessLines.how: Customers prepay by card or sign contracts of 12+ months and are charged per message, per call minute or per verification (usage), or pay one-to-three-year invoiced subscriptions in advance for Email and Segment. Twilio keeps the spread between what customers pay and what carriers and network providers charge; carrier A2P fee increases are passed through at cost, which lifts revenue and cost equally.
businessLines.description: Programmable messaging, voice, email, user authentication and identity, and the Segment customer data platform, plus phone numbers and SIP trunking, all sold through one platform.

operatingProfit.note: GAAP income from operations; margin about 3.1% (derived). FY2024 loss $(53.7)M; FY2023 loss $(876.5)M (including $320.5M impairment and $165.7M restructuring)

businessLines.name: Usage-based products: Messaging, Voice, User Authentication and Identity (Verify, Lookup)
businessLines.how: Pay-as-you-go: a fee per text or message sent or received, per minute of voice, or per verification, usually drawn down from a card prepayment with tiered volume discounts; larger customers sign commitments of at least 12 months.
businessLines.revenueNote: Not reported by product. The 10-K says the majority of revenue is usage-based, and non-usage-based fees were 26% of FY2025 revenue, so usage-based was about 74% (derived: 100% - 26%). The 26% includes Email, Segment and 'others'.

businessLines.name: Subscription products: Email (SendGrid, Marketing Campaigns) and Segment
businessLines.how: Negotiated contracts of generally one to three years, invoiced in advance and recognized evenly over the term; email sending volume tiers and the number of data sources and tracked users on Segment set the price.
businessLines.revenueNote: Not reported by product. Non-usage-based fees (subscriptions) were 26% of FY2025 revenue, 28% of FY2024 and 29% of FY2023, and 25% of Q2 2026 (10-K, 10-Q).

brands.name: Twilio SendGrid Email and Marketing Campaigns
Twilio Verify and Lookup (user authentication and identity)
Twilio.org (charitable arm, part of the company)
brands.share: Over 30,000 social impact customers used Twilio products and funding in 2025; revenue not stated
